findings.problem: The "everlasting" explanation says "Every cookie I've ever stamped is long gone." That clashes with his own world. The cookies he stamps go into sealed boxes kept for the Marriage Supper, so they aren't long gone. The line changes his mission story instead of just talking about it.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The "everlasting" and "temporary" explanations make the same joke in the same shape. Each says his cookies don't last ("Every cookie I've ever stamped is long gone" / "Temporary is a plate of my cookies sitting in front of me"), and each ends by saying the sign lasts forever ("This sign sticks around FOREVER." / "This sign lasts forever.").

rule.text: There is no formula. Each explanation sounds natural and different from the others.

findings.problem: This is still open from check2. Two explanations run 6 sentences when short fragments are counted: Stop 1 Card 4 "False" ("The fix for empty isn't trying harder. findings.question: "About 3 to 5 sentences": do short fragments count as sentences, and is 6 allowed under "about"?

findings.problem: This is still open from check2. Several explanations make up small new bakery details or one-time events: "I once spent twenty minutes looking for the spatula I was holding with my own mustache" (Stop 2 Card 5, "simpler"), "I can barely reach the top shelf over my ovens" (Stop 2 Card 5, "higher"), "my cash register would get lonely" (Stop 1 Card 2, "end"), "I can't carry a tune past the mixing bowl" (Stop 2 Card 10) and "I send a batch into the oven and sometimes it comes back as charcoal" (Stop 2 Card 8). papa-dorin.md asks for self-deprecating jokes, but it also says he "never adds anything new" to his bakery.
findings.question: Are throwaway self-deprecating bakery jokes like these allowed as personality, or do they count as adding something new to the Dorinverse? Does it matter whether a detail implies a sale (a cash register) when his bakery fills boxes for the Supper?
